title: tune-nccl-streams-and-kernel-scheduling-for-tensor-parallel-overlap-and-kv_cache
author: Chen Li
description:
Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads at production scale have been showing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local kernel compute. This causes p99 tail latency regressions under mixed request sizes and hurts throughput for steady-state batching. Additionally, KV-cache path showed increased stalls when stream priorities caused unexpected synchronization points.

This PR tunes NCCL stream usage, refactors kernel scheduling hooks, and improves KV-cache token fetch path to increase overlap between comm and compute and reduce unnecessary stream synchronization. Changes are targeted to the serving runtime in redwood/core/serving and runtime/multi_gpu modules — backwards compatible API and no model changes required.

Summary of changes:
- Introduce per-tensor-priority stream assignment for NCCL collectives so high-priority kernel work (KV-cache lookups, small attention kernels) runs on a dedicated compute stream while collectives run on separate comm streams.
- Add an opportunistic kernel pre-launch mechanism: small kernels that follow an all-reduce can be launched on a low-latency compute stream before collectives finish when dependency analysis shows safe comm/compute overlap.
- Tighten stream synchronization points to only explicit dependencies (removed broad cudaStreamSynchronize in several hot paths).
- KV-cache path changes: split blocking prefix fetch into async fetch with completion futures integrated with the serving request state machine so subsequent token generation can start earlier when cache hits are available.
- Add microbench harness and perf tests for 8/16-way tensor-parallel models (GPT-like) to guard regressions.
- New runtime knobs: TP_NCCL_STREAM_PRIORITIES, TP_KERNEL_PRELAUNCH_ENABLE, KV_CACHE_ASYNC_FETCH (default: enabled in production builds).

Performance results (end-to-end serving microbench on 16xA100 TP-8 baseline):
- Throughput: +22% steady-state throughput for batch_size=8 continuous-batch workload.
- Latency: p99 reduced by ~12% for mixed-request workloads; median latency unchanged.
- KV-cache tail: cache-hit p99 improved by ~25% for repeated-prefix traces.
- No measurable regression on single-GPU small-batch latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add per-stream priority allocation and documentation.
- [x] Implement opportunistic prelaunch logic with safety checks.
- [x] Update KV-cache fetch to async flow with state-machine integration.
- [x] Add microbench and perf CI jobs.
- [x] Run perf-canary across 8/16-GPU clusters and validate.
- [x] Add release notes.

Risk and mitigation: Changes touch low-level scheduling and NCCL usage. To mitigate risk we:
- Default new knobs to disabled in dev images, enabled in canary+prod after perf validation.
- Added thorough unit + integration coverage and a canary rollout (50% capacity) before full rollout.
- Fall back: if TP_NCCL_STREAM_PRIORITIES is disabled, runtime behavior is identical to previous releases.

Related: ENG-3891 (TP perf initiative), ENG-3970 (KV-cache tail latency). Related PRs: pr-40312-optimize-nccl-overlap-tp-kernel-scheduling.json, pr-41567-optimize-nccl-overlap-tp-collectives-and-kernel-scheduling.json

review_comments: Ava Patel: This is a big win, Chen. A couple asks: can you add a metric that tracks prelaunch success rate and how often it avoided a sync? Also add a safety gate to disable prelaunch if it causes >1% incorrect dependency detections in the canary?
Chen Li: Added prelaunch_success_rate metric and safety gate via TP_KERNEL_PRELAUNCH_SAFETY_THRESHOLD. Canary saw 0.04% false detections in our perf runs. Updated tests to assert safety threshold.
Lucas Reed: Please ensure the KV-cache async flow doesn't change semantics for cache-miss paths. Add an integration test that exercises interleaved cache-miss + collectives workloads.
Chen Li: Added integration test redwood/tests/integration/kv_cache_async_interleave_test.cc and verified local and canary runs.
Priya Shah: CI perf-canary was flaky at first (missing GPU affinity), reran and looks green now. Approving once canary is green.
Ava Patel: Approved after perf-canary results. Leaving note to watch for any increase in small-batch single-GPU latency in next days.
release_notes: Improved NCCL stream and kernel scheduling for tensor-parallel workloads, enabled async KV-cache fetch by default in production builds; expect ~20% throughput improvements on TP-heavy workloads and reduced KV-cache tail latency. Rollout via canary with runtime knobs for rollback.
notes_for_ops: New knobs: TP_NCCL_STREAM_PRIORITIES (string: low,normal,high), TP_KERNEL_PRELAUNCH_ENABLE (bool), TP_KERNEL_PRELAUNCH_SAFETY_THRESHOLD (float), KV_CACHE_ASYNC_FETCH (bool). Default enabled in prod images. If regressions observed, disable TP_KERNEL_PRELAUNCH_ENABLE and KV_CACHE_ASYNC_FETCH and redeploy. Monitor metric: prelaunch_success_rate and kv_cache_async_miss_rate.
